The most appropriate diagnostic test to confirm the diagnosis is a Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the skull. MRI is essential for visualizing brain structures and identifying any lesions or abnormalities that could explain the symptoms and papilledema. This aligns with the consensus that MRI is the preferred imaging modality in cases of suspected intracranial hypertension and related complications. Other options, such as lumbar puncture, may be considered for further evaluation but are not definitive for confirming the primary diagnosis in this context.
